chapter_seo_title: Chapter 607: The True and the False — Li Huowang Becomes a Ghost
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang faces the Heart-Pan of Doumu and is turned into a "fake"—a ghost that can't touch anything. Stuck between realities, he must learn to weaponize the Bewilderment Way or be erased forever.
og_title: Li Huowang Just Got Turned Into a Ghost
og_description: Chapter 607 of Daoguai Yixian: Our favorite broken protagonist has his reality status revoked. Can he use the Bewilderment Way to claw his way back?
twitter_title: Li Huowang is now a "fake" and can't touch anything!
twitter_description: New chapter of Daoguai Yixian: the Heart-Pan of Doumu performs an ontological exorcism. Li Huowang must become the embodiment of Bewilderment to survive.

lore_anchors.definition: A mortal who serves as a Siming's causal anchor in the world, allowing the high-dimensional entity to interact with reality. Their existence is deeply tied to the True-False Heavenly Way.
The Siming, or Mother of the Big Dipper, an entity associated with life, healing, and cosmic balance, here twisted into a terrifying source of ontological horror.
A fundamental law of the Dao-Twisted World concerned with the state of being "real" or "fake," often manipulated by the Siming and their Heart-Pans.
A specific "Heavenly Way" or cosmic law associated with Li Huowang's patron Siming, Ji Zai. It governs confusion and the breakdown of stable reality.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Li Huowang’s attacks stop working?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Heart-Pan of Doumu used a Daoist chant to make Li Huowang “fake,” an ontological ghost that can’t affect real things.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What are the red pills Li Huowang took?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The chapter doesn’t explicitly say, but they appear to be a tool or drug that re-anchors him to the Dao-Twisted World, allowing him to touch reality again.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the cruise ship scene a flashback or a projection?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It’s deliberately ambiguous. It could be a previous event, a mental projection, or a parallel reality triggered by the pills, mirroring the chapter’s theme of blurred truth.
